function_question: How does nature sink and float on purpose?

hero.name: Yuki
hero.role: Lina's friend and a young aquarium helper

opening.text: There was a girl called Yuki who helped her friend Lina at an aquarium rescue lab, where sick fish were cared for until they were strong again.
Yuki fed the fish, checked the water and watched them glide up and down the tanks without even trying.
A tiny ring fell to the bottom of the practice tank. "A hand in the water will scare the fish," Yuki said. "We need a little diver that can go down and come back up!"

card.problem: A ring is stuck at the bottom of the tank
card.goal: A diver that sinks and rises on command
card.rules: No batteries, no hands in the water

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The lost ring
chapters.line: Yuki peers into the tank and wonders: how can a toy dive down and come back up?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Yuki needs a co-pilot
chapters.line: Every submarine needs a co-pilot. Will you dive in with Yuki?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Yuki meet heroes that sink and float whenever they like.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the bubble
chapters.line: The heroes show how a little air changes everything.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training at the test glass
chapters.line: Yuki fills a glass with water and hands you a pen cap and some clay.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The why detective
chapters.line: When the diver won't dive, you ask "why?" five times to find the real reason.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great submarine starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big dive
chapters.line: The first diver just bobs on top. You find out why, fix it, and dive again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Ring rescued
chapters.line: The diver rises with the ring on its hook, and the fish never even noticed.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. A ring is stuck at the bottom of the rescue lab's tank, and Yuki needs a diver that sinks and rises on command. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a bubbly idea for making things sink and float. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Sea creatures have been diving and rising for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who control their float!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which diver will float just right, with only its tip showing? Do this over a sink or a tray.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your diver before and after the squeeze, like a real submarine designer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your bottle diver, squeeze to sink, catch the ring and let go to rise. How many seconds does one full rescue take?
guide.retry_tip: Diver not diving? Ask "why?" until you find the real reason. Change just ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, whenever something falls into a tank, the rescue lab sends down a diver like YOURS, and the fish swim on without a worry.

quick_check.question: The tank is 30 cm deep. Yuki's diver sinks 10 cm every second. How many seconds does it take to reach the ring?
quick_check.right: Right! 10 cm, 20 cm, 30 cm: that's 3 seconds to reach the bottom.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Count up in tens: after 1 second it's 10 cm down, after 2 seconds it's 20 cm…

clue_cards.name: Fish
clue_cards.trick: A swim bladder: a little bag of gas inside its body.
clue_cards.does: Adding gas makes it rise, letting some out makes it sink, so it can hover at any depth.

clue_cards.name: Nautilus
clue_cards.trick: A spiral shell with gas-filled rooms called chambers.
clue_cards.does: It moves liquid in and out of the chambers to become heavier or lighter.

clue_cards.name: Diving beetle
clue_cards.trick: A silver bubble of air tucked under its wing cases.
clue_cards.does: The bubble pulls it up, so it holds a plant to stay down and lets go to rise.

clue_cards.name: Sperm whale
clue_cards.trick: A giant head full of a special oil.
clue_cards.does: Scientists think the oil may firm up when cool and soften when warm, helping it sink and rise.

items.label: A diver whose air bubble is squeezed smaller
A fish that adds gas to its swim bladder
A submarine that lets water into its tanks

predict.explain: Less air for the same weight means heavier for its size, so it sinks. More air means lighter for its size, so it rises.

lab.title: The float-just-right lab
lab.predict: Put each pen-cap diver in a full bottle of water. Which one will sink with the gentlest squeeze and still float back up?
lab.measure: squeeze needed to sink it (1 = gentle, 5 = won't sink)

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: 5 Whys is a detective tool. You keep asking "why?" until you reach the root of a problem, not just the first answer. Today you'll use all 5 whys.

parts.name: Why 1
parts.example: 🍞 Why is the toast burnt? It stayed in the toaster too long.
parts.starter: Why does the diver stay on top? Because…

parts.name: Why 2
parts.example: 🍞 Why did it stay in too long? The toaster didn't pop up.
parts.starter: Why is it too light for its size? Because…

parts.name: Why 3
parts.example: 🍞 Why didn't it pop? The dial was turned right up.
parts.starter: Why doesn't the squeeze shrink the bubble enough? Because…

parts.name: Why 4
parts.what: Keep digging: don't stop at the easy answer.
parts.example: 🍞 Why was the dial up? Someone made crumpets before.
parts.starter: Why is my squeeze getting lost? Because…

parts.name: Why 5
parts.what: Reach the root cause and fix THAT.
parts.example: 🍞 Root cause: nobody checks the dial. Fix: check it every time!
parts.starter: The root cause is… so I will fix it by…

sketch_checklist: I drew my diver in the bottle before and after the squeeze.
I labelled the air pocket, the water, the weight and the hook.
I drew arrows to show how the air bubble changes.

test.measure: seconds to sink and come back up
test.check_question: Hover check: can your diver stop halfway down?

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your diver?
